name: food-web
title: Food chain / food web
tagline: Food chain / web — organisms joined by energy-flow arrows (prey → predator); trophic levels, roles and remove-a-species knock-on all derived; labels and roles occludable.
description: A food chain or food web: organisms drawn as boxes joined by directed arrows meaning "energy flows to" / "is eaten by" — drawn prey → predator, the direction of energy flow (a common exam trap the model can label with a legend). You author only the organisms (id + label, and the one decomposer flag) and the feeding pairs (from the prey to the consumer); the model derives each organism's trophic level (producer = level 1; a consumer sits one level above the highest thing it eats), its trophic role (producer, primary / secondary / tertiary / quaternary consumer, apex predator, decomposer), the layered layout with producers at the base and energy rising, every arrow route, and — the knock-on prediction — which populations rise or fall when an organism is removed (its prey rise, its predators fall). There is nowhere to author a trophic label, so the roles cannot be wrong. Occlude an organism's label ("which organism is the producer?"), occlude its derived role readout ("name a secondary consumer"), highlight to mark an answer, colour boxes by level, and set remove to show the consequence of losing a species. Handles a simple linear chain and a branching web (multiple producers, a decomposer fed from several levels). For the energy / biomass / numbers pyramid with 10% transfer figures use diagram/pyramid; for a free labelled relationship graph use diagram/concept-map.
whenToUse: Reach for this for food chains and food webs — the GCSE / KS3 ecology topic of who eats whom, trophic levels and interdependence. Author the organisms as `organisms` (each an id + a label; add kind:"decomposer" for bacteria / fungi / worms) and the feeding relationships as `arrows`, each running `from` the prey (energy source) `to` the consumer — so "a fox eats a rabbit" is { from:"rabbit", to:"fox" }. The arrow is DRAWN prey → predator, the direction energy flows; this is the exam convention (pupils commonly draw it backwards), and show.convention (default on) prints a one-line legend saying so. Every trophic level and role is derived from the graph: a producer eats nothing (no incoming arrow); a primary consumer eats a producer; each further level is one above the highest thing it eats; an apex predator is a consumer nothing eats; a decomposer is the flagged organism. Keep the arrows in energy-flow order and the roles come out right — there is no role to author. Questions: occlude an organism's label to ask "which organism goes here?", occlude its role readout (occludeRole, with show.roles on) to ask "what is the producer? / name a secondary consumer"; highlight an organism or an arrow to mark the answer or trace one energy path. Set remove:"<id>" to predict a knock-on: the removed organism greys out, its prey are marked rising (↑) and its predators falling (↓) — a first-order prediction; deeper cascades belong in the block text. Set colorByLevel:true to tint each box by its trophic level (producers green at the base up to the apex). Staged build via reveal: grow the chain one organism at a time, reveal the roles, or reveal the knock-on last. Conventions: a food CHAIN is just a web with one arrow per organism; keep layout consistent across a lesson. Synonyms a teacher might use: food chain, food web, trophic level, producer, consumer, herbivore, carnivore, predator, prey, apex predator, decomposer, energy transfer, energy flow, interdependence, ecosystem, "who eats whom". Switch model when the picture changes: the energy / biomass / numbers pyramid with percentage transfer is diagram/pyramid; a free concept graph where each arrow carries its own written relationship is diagram/concept-map.

id.description: Unique kebab-case id for this organism, referenced by the feeding arrows (e.g. "grass", "rabbit", "fox"). Not shown to pupils — it is the wiring handle.

label.description: The organism written inside the box, wrapped to fit (e.g. "Grass", "Rabbit", "Fungi"). A noun / noun phrase.

kind.description: Mark this organism a DECOMPOSER (bacteria, fungi, worms — feeds on dead matter across all levels). This is the ONE role that cannot be derived from the feeding graph (a decomposer that is also a graph sink looks like an apex predator), so it is authored. Omit for every other organism — producer / consumer roles are all derived from position.

occlude.description: Render this organism's LABEL as "?" — the "which organism goes here?" hook. The box, its arrows and its derived role stay drawn; the hidden name never leaks into the aria. Default false.

occludeRole.description: Render this organism's derived ROLE readout as "?" — the "what is the producer? / name a secondary consumer" hook (only meaningful when show.roles is on). The label stays visible; the role word never leaks into the aria. Independent of occlude. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this organism — the answer, or the organism a staged build is drawing attention to. Default false.

organisms.description: The organisms of the chain / web. Each has a unique id and a label; add kind:"decomposer" for a decomposer. Order does not matter — positions are derived from the feeding arrows.

from.description: Id of the organism energy flows FROM — the PREY / food (the one being eaten). The arrow is drawn starting here.

to.description: Id of the organism energy flows TO — the CONSUMER / predator (the one doing the eating). The arrowhead points here. So "a rabbit eats grass" is { from: "grass", to: "rabbit" } — the arrow runs grass → rabbit, the direction of energy flow (the exam convention).

highlight.description: Amber this arrow — trace one energy path through the web. Default false.

arrows.description: The feeding relationships, each an arrow FROM the prey (energy source) TO the consumer — drawn prey → predator, the direction of energy flow. An organism can be the `to` of several arrows (eats several things) and the `from` of several (is eaten by several). A single chain is one arrow leaving each organism.

remove.description: Id of an organism to REMOVE — the knock-on hook. It is drawn greyed and struck through, its prey (what it ate) are marked rising ↑ and its predators (what ate it) marked falling ↓ — the derived first-order consequence of losing that species. Omit for the intact web.

reveal.description: Staged build: draw only the first N organisms (in trophic order, producers first) and the arrows between them. The layout is computed from the FULL web so nothing reflows as organisms appear. Omit (or 0-and-up beyond the count) to draw the whole web.

colorByLevel.description: Tint each organism box by its derived trophic level (producers green at the base, rising through the levels) — helps pupils see the levels. Default false: neutral grey boxes so the arrows carry the eye. Ignored on a removed / highlighted / rising / falling box (those colours are reserved).

layout.description: Reading direction. "vertical" (default): trophic levels stack, producers at the base, energy rising up the page. "horizontal": levels run left → right, producers on the left — natural for a simple linear food chain. Keep it consistent across a lesson.

roles.description: Show each organism's derived trophic-role readout under its box ("Producer", "Secondary consumer", "Apex predator", "Decomposer"). Default true. Turn off for a bare web where the roles are the discussion, not the answer.

levels.description: Draw a faint "Trophic level 1 / 2 / 3…" guide beside each band. Default false.

convention.description: Show the one-line legend naming the arrow convention ("Arrows point from prey to predator — the direction energy flows"). Default true — it labels the exam trap. Turn off once a class knows it.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

examples.label: Worked food web — roles labelled, arrows show energy flow
Occluded question — name the producer / a secondary consumer (roles hidden)
Blank answer space — draw the arrows / no roles
Hard case — remove-a-species knock-on (remove the fox: rabbits rise, nothing above falls)
